practices.title: Drip Pricing
practices.description: Advertising a base price while progressively revealing mandatory fees during checkout, so the final total far exceeds the price the user committed to.
practices.domains: Airlines (baggage, seat fees), hotels (resort fees), event ticketing, e-commerce, travel

practices.title: Hidden Mandatory Fees
practices.description: Adding non-optional service, facility, processing, regulatory, or "amenity" fees not disclosed alongside the headline price.
practices.domains: Hospitality, ride-hailing, telecom, fitness, real estate (junk fees), wedding planning

practices.title: Sneak-into-Basket
practices.description: Auto-adding items, insurance, warranties, donations, or services to a cart that the user must explicitly remove.
practices.domains: E-commerce, travel booking, ticketing, financial services

practices.title: Hidden Surcharges & Stacking
practices.description: Layering numerous small fees (fuel, residential, peak, accessorial) so the final invoice is opaque even to attentive customers.
practices.domains: Shipping & freight, food delivery, logistics, waste management, energy utilities

practices.title: Foreign Transaction Opacity
practices.description: Burying currency-conversion markups or international fees in fine print rather than disclosing at point of sale.

practices.title: Dynamic-Currency Conversion Markup
practices.description: Offering on-the-fly currency conversion at unfavorable rates without disclosing the markup, so users unwittingly pay above-market exchange.

practices.title: Crisis-Period Price Gouging
practices.description: Algorithmically raising prices on essential goods or services during emergencies, weather events, or supply shocks when consumers cannot defer purchase.
practices.domains: Grocery, e-commerce, ride-hailing, food delivery, plumbing/home repair, pest control

practices.title: Emergency-Markup Exploitation
practices.description: Charging premium rates for after-hours, urgent, or emergency service when the customer has no time to compare alternatives.
practices.domains: Plumbing, automotive towing, veterinary, healthcare, funeral services, cybersecurity (ransomware response)

practices.title: Last-Minute Price Inflation
practices.description: Raising prices dramatically as the deadline (travel date, event, deadline) approaches, exploiting urgency.

practices.title: Algorithmic Personalized Pricing
practices.description: Adjusting prices in real time based on browsing history, device, location, or perceived willingness to pay without disclosure.
practices.domains: Hospitality, e-commerce, ride-hailing, grocery, fashion, ticketing

practices.title: Tourist-Targeted Overcharging
practices.description: Charging higher prices to visibly identifiable visitors who lack local knowledge of fair prices, sometimes refusing meters or quoting opaque flat rates.
practices.domains: Taxi services, retail in tourist zones, hospitality, currency exchange

practices.title: Bait Pricing
practices.description: Advertising a price or product that is unavailable, then steering the customer to a more expensive alternative.
practices.domains: Real estate, automotive sales, e-commerce, cleaning services, home services

practices.title: Yo-Yo Financing
practices.description: Letting a customer take possession after a sale, then claiming financing fell through to impose worse terms.

practices.title: Underbid-and-Inflate
practices.description: Submitting a low bid to win a contract, then recovering margin through change orders, "unforeseen conditions," or scope creep.

practices.title: Allowance Underspecification
practices.description: Setting unrealistically low material or service allowances in a quote, knowing the customer will exceed them and pay the difference.

practices.title: Diagnostic-to-Repair Conversion
practices.description: Advertising free or low-cost diagnostics that convert into expensive repair commitments without re-quoting.

practices.title: Vendor Substitution
practices.description: Replacing the contracted vendor or specified material with a lower-cost alternative while charging the original rate.
practices.domains: Wedding planning, construction, dental (lab work), beauty (formulation)

practices.title: Renewal-Time Feature Downgrade
practices.description: Removing or restricting features included in the prior term and offering them only at a higher tier upon renewal.
practices.domains: Cloud / SaaS, streaming, mobile carriers, fitness

practices.title: Material/Parts Markup Concealment
practices.description: Charging retail or inflated prices for materials, parts, or supplies while presenting prices as "at cost" or omitting markup disclosure.
practices.domains: Plumbing, home services, dental (lab work), veterinary, cleaning, automotive repair

practices.title: Apprentice-at-Journeyman Rate
practices.description: Billing senior-level rates while assigning the work to junior, unqualified, or apprentice personnel.
practices.domains: Consulting, legal services, plumbing, accounting & auditing

practices.title: Billable-Hour Inflation
practices.description: Padding hours through unnecessary meetings, redundant research, or rounded entries.

practices.title: Expense Padding
practices.description: Inflating travel, accommodation, and operational expenses passed through to clients beyond actual cost.

practices.title: Flat-Rate Pricing Opacity
practices.description: Quoting flat rates that vastly exceed the time-and-materials cost without disclosing the calculation, hiding effective hourly rates.

practices.title: Mini-Bar / Incidentals Gouging
practices.description: Charging extreme markups (often 300–800%) on captive in-room or in-venue items, sometimes with sensor-based auto-billing for items merely moved.
practices.domains: Hotels, event venues, hospitality, pet industry (in-clinic prescriptions)

practices.title: Wedding/Occasion Tax
practices.description: Charging more for identical services when labeled with a high-emotion event (wedding, funeral) than for an ordinary "event."

practices.title: MSRP Inflation for Discount Illusion
practices.description: Setting artificially high "manufacturer suggested retail prices" so retailers can advertise large but illusory discounts.

practices.title: Outlet-Store Deception
practices.description: Manufacturing lower-quality goods specifically for outlet channels while implying they are excess or overstock from the main line.

practices.title: Captive-Venue Concession Markup
practices.description: Charging extreme markups on essential items (food, water, basic snacks) inside venues where consumers cannot leave and return, often selling commodity items at 5–10× retail.
practices.domains: Theme parks, sports stadiums, concert venues, cinemas, airports (post-security), cruise ships

practices.title: Outside-Food / Drink Prohibition
practices.description: Banning patrons from bringing essential items (water, food, baby formula) into a venue specifically to channel demand into overpriced concessions, sometimes confiscating items at entry.
practices.domains: Theme parks, sports stadiums, concert venues, cinemas

practices.title: Cultural-Practice Pricing-Out
practices.description: Inflating prices on items central to a society's customary rituals (shared meals, gathering venues, holiday foods) well beyond cost basis, making the cultural practice economically inaccessible while continuing to market the venue or product as part of that ritual.
practices.domains: Restaurants (American social-eating culture), event venues, holiday-food retail, "third place" cafes

practices.title: Price Creep
practices.description: Gradual, repeated price increases above inflation, exploiting customer inertia and switching costs.
practices.domains: SaaS, streaming, insurance, mobile carriers, cleaning services

practices.title: Loyalty Penalty
practices.description: Charging long-term customers more than new customers for identical coverage or service.

practices.title: Teaser-Rate Trap
practices.description: Offering low introductory pricing that escalates dramatically after the first renewal cycle.
practices.domains: Insurance, mobile carriers, cosmetics (subscription), gym memberships

practices.title: Auto-Renewal Price Hike
practices.description: Renewing a subscription at a higher price than the prior term without explicit consent or prominent advance notice.
practices.domains: Cloud/SaaS, streaming, cybersecurity, fitness, dating, telecom

practices.title: Mile / Point Devaluation
practices.description: Unilaterally reducing the value, redemption availability, or expiration window of accumulated loyalty points or miles.
practices.domains: Airlines, hotels, retail loyalty programs, credit-card rewards

practices.title: Shrinkflation
practices.description: Reducing product quantity, weight, or volume while keeping price (and often packaging) the same, without conspicuous disclosure.
practices.domains: Grocery, food/beverage manufacturing, cosmetics, personal care

practices.title: Silent Quality Degradation
practices.description: Reducing fabric weight, material grade, ingredient quality, or build standard while maintaining or increasing price without disclosure.
practices.domains: Fashion, food manufacturing, dental (material grade), home appliances

practices.title: Substitute Ingredient Swap
practices.description: Quietly replacing a higher-quality ingredient with a cheaper alternative without updating packaging or notifying consumers.

practices.title: Unit-Price Manipulation
practices.description: Displaying unit prices in inconsistent units (per ounce vs. per pound, per use vs. per package) so cross-product comparison is impractical.

practices.title: Serving-Size Manipulation
practices.description: Defining unrealistically small serving sizes so per-serving nutritional or alcohol-content figures appear favorable.

practices.title: Glazing / Weight-Padding
practices.description: Over-glazing frozen products with ice or otherwise inflating sale weight beyond accepted limits.

practices.title: Checkout-Scanner Discrepancy
practices.description: Shelf and scanned prices disagree, consistently in the seller's favor.

practices.title: Overdraft Reordering
practices.description: Processing transactions largest-first to maximize overdraft fees, cascading charges from small purchases.

practices.title: Payday-Loan / Refund-Advance Trap
practices.description: Offering short-term loans at effective APRs above 100–300%, designed for rollover rather than repayment, often disguised as "instant refunds."

practices.title: Penalty-APR Weaponization
practices.description: Applying penalty rates to entire balances after a single late payment, including new purchases.

practices.title: Minimum-Payment Illusion
practices.description: Displaying minimum payments prominently while burying total interest cost and time-to-payoff.

practices.title: Negative-Equity Rolling
practices.description: Rolling negative equity from a previous loan into a new loan without clearly disclosing the increased total obligation.

practices.title: Debt-Trap Lending
practices.description: Extending credit, leases, or input loans with terms designed to create perpetual financial dependency.
practices.domains: Agriculture (farmer debt), cannabis (grower lending), debt collection, prison commissary

practices.title: Refund-Advance APR Concealment
practices.description: Marketing refund anticipation loans as "instant refunds" while obscuring effective interest rates that often exceed 100% APR.

practices.title: Pre-Need Investment Misrepresentation
practices.description: Marketing pre-paid funeral or cemetery products as appreciating financial investments rather than prepaid services.

practices.title: Payment-Plan Predatory Terms
practices.description: Offering high-interest installment plans for essential expenditures without disclosing total interest paid.

practices.title: Bill Cramming
practices.description: Adding unauthorized charges — third-party services, premium SMS, mystery fees — to invoices without explicit consent.

practices.title: Estimated-Billing Overcharge
practices.description: Systematically estimating bills on the high side rather than from actual meter or usage data, requiring customers to identify and dispute.

practices.title: Damage-Claim Fabrication
practices.description: Charging customers for pre-existing damage, normal wear, or fabricated incidents after departure without dispute opportunity.
practices.domains: Hospitality, automotive (lease return), real estate (security deposits)

practices.title: Inactivity / Maintenance Drain
practices.description: Charging maintenance or inactivity fees that slowly drain dormant accounts to zero.
practices.domains: Financial services, gift cards, fashion (gift balances)

practices.title: Zombie Subscription Charging
practices.description: Continuing to bill after cancellation or account deletion by retaining payment tokens and citing "billing-cycle completion."
practices.domains: Fitness, dating, cleaning services, cosmetics, financial services

practices.title: Coordination-of-Benefits Fraud
practices.description: Billing multiple insurers for the full allowed amount rather than coordinating, resulting in overpayment or balance billing.

practices.title: Insurance Code Upcoding
practices.description: Coding procedures at higher reimbursement levels than clinically warranted to inflate insurance billing.

practices.title: Pre-Selected Default Tip Percentages
practices.description: POS terminals defaulting to high tip percentages (often 18–30%), placing the no-tip option in a smaller, lower-contrast, or extra-tap location, or pre-highlighting the largest amount.
practices.domains: Counter-service food, retail, mobile POS systems, ride-hailing apps

practices.title: Tip Solicitation Outside Service Contexts
practices.description: Soliciting tips in transactions historically not tipped — self-checkout, take-out, retail, automated kiosks — exploiting social pressure and unfamiliarity to extract gratuities for services that involve no traditional service component.
practices.domains: Retail, self-checkout, automated kiosks, take-out food, airport concessions

practices.title: Tip-on-Tax / Tip-on-Pre-Discount Total
practices.description: Calculating suggested tip percentages on the tax-inclusive total or pre-discount price, inflating the displayed "suggested" amount above the cost of the underlying service.

practices.title: Asymmetric Signup/Cancel
practices.description: Allowing instant online signup while requiring phone calls, certified mail, or in-person visits to cancel.
practices.domains: Fitness/gyms, dating, gambling, cosmetics, cleaning, mental health, telecom

practices.title: Cancellation Maze
practices.description: Designing multi-step cancellation flows with confusing portals, hidden links, or repeated confirmation steps.
practices.domains: Fitness, dating, mobile carriers, food delivery, streaming, dental insurance

practices.title: Retention Dark Patterns
practices.description: Mandatory retention calls, guilt-tripping prompts, repeated "are you sure?" friction, or hidden cancel buttons that pressure users to stay.
practices.domains: Streaming, fitness, cybersecurity, mental health, news subscriptions

practices.title: Zombie Billing Post-Cancel
practices.description: Continuing to charge after a cancellation has been requested, citing "processing periods" or "billing-cycle completion."

practices.title: Cooling-Off Period Removal
practices.description: Eliminating any post-sale cancellation window even when the user has not yet used the service.
practices.domains: Telecom, fitness, real estate (leases), wedding planning

practices.title: Hidden Renewal
practices.description: Auto-renewing subscriptions or contracts without prominent advance notice, banking on user inattention.
practices.domains: Streaming, telecom, fitness, dating, supplements, pest control, waste management

practices.title: Free-Trial Conversion Trap
practices.description: Collecting payment information for "free" trials and silently converting to paid at the end of the trial without notification.

practices.title: Auto-Renewal with Escalation
practices.description: Automatically renewing into a new long-term commitment at a higher price or expanded scope without affirmative consent.
practices.domains: Cleaning services, waste management, fitness, telecom

practices.title: Renewal Pressure Tactics
practices.description: Using urgency, fear messaging, or artificial deadlines at renewal to upgrade or rebind.

practices.title: Silent Coverage Erosion
practices.description: Renewing policies or contracts with reduced coverage at the same or higher price without highlighting the changes.

practices.title: Tier Degradation
practices.description: Moving features previously included in a tier to a higher-priced tier (or removing them altogether).

practices.title: Feature Gating of Existing Hardware
practices.description: Software-disabling capabilities present in already-purchased hardware to justify a premium tier.
practices.domains: Home appliances, automotive (over-the-air feature removal), connected devices

practices.title: Subscription Requirements for Core Functions
practices.description: Requiring ongoing payment for features that were one-time purchases or that cost nothing to deliver.
practices.domains: Home appliances, automotive (heated seats subscription), gaming (always-online DRM)

practices.title: Ad Injection into Paid Tiers
practices.description: Adding advertising to previously ad-free tiers, then offering ad removal at a higher price.

practices.title: Ad-Tier Bait-and-Switch
practices.description: Introducing a low-cost ad-supported tier whose ad load progressively increases over time.

practices.title: Quality Throttling of Free Tier
practices.description: Deliberately degrading the free or low-tier experience to manufacture urgency for upgrade.
practices.domains: Dating (match visibility), gaming, e-commerce search, social media reach

practices.title: Microtransaction Fatigue
practices.description: Requiring per-action payments (super likes, boosts, premium reactions) that accumulate beyond the advertised subscription cost.

practices.title: Grind-or-Pay Design
practices.description: Intentionally slowing free progression to push players or users toward paid shortcuts.

practices.title: Proprietary-Format Lock-In
practices.description: Storing user data in proprietary formats with no documented open alternative, making migration prohibitively costly.
practices.domains: Cloud/SaaS, healthcare (EHR), automotive (telematics), cybersecurity, music industry

practices.title: Data-Export Obstruction
practices.description: Imposing technical or bureaucratic obstacles — throttled exports, mandatory tickets, complex transformations — that make leaving impractical.

practices.title: Egress / Data-Out Fees
practices.description: Setting data-export or transfer fees far exceeding actual cost, financially penalizing departure.

practices.title: Punitive Early-Termination Fees
practices.description: Imposing exit penalties that exceed the cost of staying, including full remaining-contract payment.
practices.domains: Mobile carriers, cloud/SaaS, real estate, fitness, gym, waste management

practices.title: API Deprecation Without Migration
practices.description: Deprecating APIs critical to customer integrations without providing migration paths, replacements, or adequate notice.

practices.title: Ecosystem Identity Lock-In
practices.description: Requiring use of the provider's identity, authentication, or management services across all products, making partial migration infeasible.

practices.title: Parts Pairing / Component DRM
practices.description: Using software locks or serialization that prevent third-party or self-installed parts from functioning even when physically compatible.
practices.domains: Automotive, home appliances, agriculture (tractors), medical devices

practices.title: Carrier Unlock Obstruction
practices.description: Maintaining device locks beyond the contract period or imposing fees / bureaucracy to unlock paid-off devices.

practices.title: Number Porting Obstruction
practices.description: Delaying, gating, or routing number-port requests through retention pressure to discourage carrier switching.

practices.title: Open-Source Bait-and-Switch
practices.description: Building market position on open-source releases, then transitioning core capabilities to proprietary or closed licenses once dominant.

practices.title: Tying of Unwanted Products
practices.description: Requiring purchase of unrelated products or services as a condition of obtaining the desired one.
practices.domains: Insurance, financial services, e-commerce, agriculture (seed-herbicide bundling)

practices.title: Mandatory Bundle Pricing
practices.description: Offering only bundled packages that mix essential and optional items so individual costs cannot be compared.
practices.domains: Funeral services, wedding planning, event ticketing, cable/internet

practices.title: Bundle Obfuscation
practices.description: Bundling multiple services so individual pricing and partial cancellation are obscured.

practices.title: Cloud-Service Bundling
practices.description: Bundling infrastructure, platform, and SaaS products to foreclose competitors of any single layer.

practices.title: Mandatory Arbitration Clause
practices.description: Requiring arbitration in EULAs, employment contracts, or service terms that strips users or workers of access to courts and class actions.
practices.domains: Financial services, gaming (EULAs), tobacco, internal company ethics, gig economy

practices.title: Operator-Friendly Forum Selection
practices.description: Forcing arbitration in jurisdictions chosen for operator advantage, with short complaint windows and limited discovery.

practices.title: EULA Retroactive Modification
practices.description: Unilaterally changing EULAs or terms after purchase to reduce user rights or expand data collection.

practices.title: Unilateral Contract Changes
practices.description: Modifying agreement terms (commission, fees, scope) with minimal notice, forcing take-it-or-leave-it acceptance.
practices.domains: E-commerce platforms, food delivery, gig economy, app stores

practices.title: Force-Majeure Asymmetry
practices.description: Drafting force-majeure clauses that protect the vendor but not the customer.

practices.title: Punitive Cancellation Penalty
practices.description: Imposing cancellation penalties disproportionate to actual lost revenue.

practices.title: Non-Refundable Trap
practices.description: Defaulting to non-refundable bookings while making refundable options hard to find or significantly more expensive.

practices.title: Concession Clawback
practices.description: Offering "first month free" promotions whose cost is recovered through inflated base rent or fees over the lease term.

practices.title: Lien Threats
practices.description: Filing or threatening mechanic's liens to coerce payment for disputed or incomplete work.

practices.title: Hidden Costs at Checkout
practices.description: Revealing fees only on the final step of checkout, after the user has invested time in the flow.

practices.title: Sneak into Basket
practices.description: Pre-selecting or auto-adding items, insurance, donations, or services to a cart.

practices.title: Disguised Ads
practices.description: Designing ads to look like content, navigation, or organic recommendations.
practices.domains: Search engines, e-commerce, social media, news

practices.title: Bait & Switch (Outcome)
practices.description: Promising one outcome (free download, simple signup) and delivering a different one (subscription, account creation).

practices.title: Fake Countdown Timer
practices.description: Displaying a countdown that resets, has no real consequence, or is decorative.

practices.title: False Scarcity
practices.description: Showing inventory levels ("only 2 left") or claims of scarcity ("limited release") that are fabricated or manufactured.

practices.title: Fake Social Proof
practices.description: Showing "47 people viewing this" or similar figures that are randomized or fabricated.

practices.title: Manufactured Emotional Urgency
practices.description: Notifications like "Someone special is waiting" or "Your match expires soon" designed to provoke immediate action.

practices.title: In-Play Bet Time-Pressure
practices.description: Countdown windows on in-play betting that rush bettors into rapid wagers without deliberation.

practices.title: Confirmshaming
practices.description: Using guilt-inducing or self-deprecating language for the opt-out option ("No thanks, I don't want to save money").

practices.title: Visual Interference
practices.description: Using contrast, size, or position to obscure the option that disadvantages the platform (tiny gray "decline" links, prominent "Yes" buttons).

practices.title: Trick Questions
practices.description: Confusing double negatives or unclear toggle states ("Uncheck to not receive newsletters").

practices.title: Pre-Checked Boxes
practices.description: Defaulting to opt-in for marketing, data sharing, or ancillary purchases.

practices.title: Roach Motel
practices.description: Easy entry, hard exit (see also § 2.1).
practices.domains: Subscriptions, gym memberships, dating, mental health, gambling

practices.title: Privacy Zuckering
practices.description: Defaulting privacy controls to maximum data sharing and burying granular controls in obscure menus.
practices.domains: Social media, search engines, mobile OSes

practices.title: Price-Comparison Prevention
practices.description: Designing tiers, features, or measurements so cross-product or cross-vendor comparison is impractical.
practices.domains: Telecom plans, insurance, energy tariffs, hospitality (resort fees)

practices.title: Cookie-Consent Dark Patterns
practices.description: Pre-selected options, hidden reject buttons, confusing toggle UIs, or bury-the-decline patterns.

practices.title: Forced Registration
practices.description: Requiring account creation for actions that don't need persistent identity (viewing prices, completing a one-time purchase).

practices.title: Forced Continuity
practices.description: Automatic conversion of a free trial to paid without a clear pre-charge prompt.

practices.title: Friend Spam / Contact Upload
practices.description: Requiring contact-list access or social-graph permissions as a condition of basic functionality.

practices.title: Forced Ad Targeting
practices.description: Making personalized ad targeting a non-negotiable condition of using the service, even in paid tiers.

practices.title: Aggressive In-Person Solicitation
practices.description: Verbal solicitation, shouting, harassment, or physical blocking of potential customers in transit hubs and tourist zones to coerce a transaction before they can compare alternatives.
practices.domains: Taxi services at airports/stations, timeshare reps, street vendors

practices.title: Variable Reward Scheduling
practices.description: Unpredictable rewards (likes, matches, drops) tuned to maximize engagement, mirroring slot-machine mechanics.

practices.title: Infinite Scroll
practices.description: Eliminating natural stopping cues by paginating endlessly.

practices.title: Autoplay
practices.description: Auto-advancing to the next video, episode, or content item without user action.

practices.title: Notification Manipulation
practices.description: Strategic alerts ("You have unseen activity!") designed to trigger re-engagement when nothing new is present.

practices.title: Streak Mechanics
practices.description: Punishing breaks in usage with public streak loss and reminders.

practices.title: Artificial Progress Bars
practices.description: Profile or task completeness indicators that exploit completion bias and never quite reach 100%.

practices.title: Pull-to-Refresh as Slot Lever
practices.description: Gesture-based feed refresh that mimics slot-machine pulls with variable new content.

practices.title: Loss-Disguised-as-Win Cues
practices.description: Celebrating near-misses or partial returns with winning sounds, animations, or visual cues that neurologically mimic actual wins.

practices.title: Time-Distortion Design
practices.description: Removing clocks, windows, or natural time cues to obscure session duration.

practices.title: Fear Appeals
practices.description: Marketing that exaggerates risks ("Your data is at risk!") to drive action.
practices.domains: Cybersecurity, supplements, baby products, insurance, pet industry, home services

practices.title: Guilt Induction
practices.description: Implying the user is letting someone down by declining ("You'll regret this," "Don't you care?").

practices.title: Social-Pressure Framing
practices.description: Implying social judgment ("Your friends already joined").

practices.title: Loss Framing
practices.description: Emphasizing what the user will lose ("Don't lose your progress!").

practices.title: False Authority Claims
practices.description: Fabricated or unsubstantiated expert endorsements ("Recommended by 9/10 doctors").

practices.title: Dignity-Language Exploitation
practices.description: Steering grieving or vulnerable customers toward expensive options through implied judgments about love, respect, or duty.
practices.domains: Funeral services, senior care, wedding planning

practices.title: Outrage Amplification
practices.description: Algorithmically prioritizing anger-inducing or divisive content because it maximizes engagement.

practices.title: Polarization Optimization
practices.description: Optimizing recommendations to reinforce existing beliefs and suppress cross-cutting perspectives.

practices.title: Calm-Content Demotion
practices.description: Down-ranking informational content that does not provoke strong emotional responses.

practices.title: Fringe-Content Amplification
practices.description: Promoting extreme, conspiratorial, or sensational content because it generates longer sessions.

practices.title: Self-Harm Content Clustering
practices.description: Algorithmically recommending or clustering self-harm, eating-disorder, or suicide content to vulnerable users.

practices.title: Excessive Data Collection
practices.description: Gathering more data than is necessary for the stated purpose.
practices.domains: Cross-domain (mobile apps, automotive infotainment, smart appliances, fitness, gaming)

practices.title: Purpose Creep
practices.description: Using data collected for one purpose ("service improvement") for unrelated purposes (ad targeting, employee evaluation, partner deals) without renewed consent.
practices.domains: Internal company ethics, social media, telecom, healthcare

practices.title: Cloud-Dependency Coercion
practices.description: Requiring cloud connectivity for core product functionality so data collection becomes a precondition of operation.

practices.title: Phoning Home Without Purpose
practices.description: Software transmitting telemetry to company servers when no cloud feature is needed for the product to function.
practices.domains: Operating systems, productivity software, smart appliances

practices.title: Infotainment / Synced-Phone Harvesting
practices.description: Collecting contacts, calendar entries, text messages, or media from a connected phone without clear disclosure.

practices.title: Shadow Profiling
practices.description: Building behavioral, demographic, or social-graph profiles of individuals who have never created accounts, via pixels, contact uploads, or third-party data.
practices.domains: Social media, advertising, data brokers, internal company ethics

practices.title: Public-Records Aggregation Profiling
practices.description: Combining disparate public records — court filings, deeds, voter rolls — into invasive composite profiles.

practices.title: Inferred-Attribute Profiling
practices.description: Using algorithms to infer protected or sensitive characteristics (health conditions, sexuality, religion, immigration status) from behavioral data.

practices.title: Cross-Site Tracking Without Consent
practices.description: Following users across sites and apps via tracking pixels, device graphs, or identifier sharing.

practices.title: Browser & Canvas Fingerprinting
practices.description: Using browser, canvas, or device fingerprinting to circumvent cookie restrictions and re-identify users who have cleared cookies.

practices.title: Cross-Device Identity Stitching
practices.description: Linking activity across a user's phone, tablet, and desktop into unified profiles without explicit consent.

practices.title: Cross-Product Data Fusion
practices.description: Merging data across multiple products of the same vendor into unified profiles without product-specific consent.

practices.title: Cross-Service Data Sharing
practices.description: Using customer data from one service to benefit another service in the provider's portfolio without explicit consent.

practices.title: Background Location Tracking
